recipes.name: Minecraft Cake inspired by Minecraft
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together whole eggs, egg yolks, milk, and vanilla paste. Set aside. - ~3 large eggs - ~7 egg yolks - 240 g whole milk - 1 tbsp vanilla paste
In a stand mixer, combine cake flour, sugar, baking powder, and kosher salt. - 550 g cake flour - 550 g sugar - 1 tbsp baking powder - 2 tbsp kosher salt
Gradually add softened unsalted butter to the dry ingredients, mixing until pebbly in texture. - 350 g unsalted butter softened
Slowly add the wet mixture in thirds to the dry mixture, combining fully after each addition. - For the Cake Batter
Pour the batter into a greased square cake pan and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 60-70 minutes until golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean. - For the Cake Batter

In a saucepan, combine raspberries, sugar, and the juice of ½ lemon. Cook until the berries break down. Strain through a sieve, then dissolve powdered gelatin mixed with sugar into the warm mixture. Spread on a mat and refrigerate until set. - 12 oz rasberries - 2 ½ oz sugar - ½ lemon juiced - 1 packet of powdered gelatin - ½ oz sugar
Whip large egg yolks in a stand mixer until pale and ribbon-y. - 6 large egg yolks
Meanwhile, bring water and sugar to a boil. Let it cool slightly, then slowly add to the egg yolks while whipping. - 2 oz water - 7 oz sugar - 6 large egg yolks

Gradually add sticks of softened butter, mixing until smooth. Flavor with vanilla extract, salt, and fold in melted white chocolate. - 4 (453 g)sticks unsalted butter (room temperature) - 1 tsp vanilla extract - ½ tsp salt - 6 oz white chocolate (melted)

Spread the buttercream evenly on the cooled cake, trimming the top for a flat surface. Cut the sweet berry coulis into squares and arrange them on top to mimic the iconic "Minecraft" cake. - For the Cake Batter - For the Buttercream Frosting
